sourceAttempts.family: Bureau of Land Management Rio Chama page
sourceAttempts.result: BLM documents high demand, the 22-mile El Vado Ranch–Chavez Canyon wilderness section, the lower Chavez–Big Eddy section, permits, camping, access management and the direct below-El-Vado flow station.

BLM rates Rio Chama Class II–III, publishes 22¼, 8¼ and 31-mile distances, named designated launches/take-outs, road caveats and a recommended 300 cfs minimum for kayaks, canoes and rafts under 12 ft.
USGS 08285500 is the direct Rio Chama below El Vado Dam discharge station used for minimum-flow scoring.

El Vado coordinates are from the BLM access page; Chavez Canyon and Big Eddy coordinates are mapped public water-entry anchors cross-checked against local ramp/geology records and remain review-level for field confirmation.
Selected Rio Chama River.jpg, a same-river New Mexico photograph by Matt Walter via Wikimedia Commons under CC BY 2.0.

thresholdEvidence.reachApplicability: BLM recommends at least 300 cfs for kayaks, canoes and rafts under 12 ft; larger rafts have a 500 cfs recommendation. Flows vary with releases, irrigation and rain.
